name: Henle First Year Latin
_note: grammar: the lesson in which each form is first taught, taken from the table of contents of Henle, First Year Latin (1958 printing). The typed games open a row or column once the lesson filter reaches that number. A tense is a single lesson number, or a map by conjugation where Henle teaches it one conjugation at a time. null means the form is never taught in this book. Compounds follow their base verb (absum like sum, adeō like eō).

_source.L1-5: the five declensions, one per lesson; L6 nouns with special meanings in the plural
_source.L7: adjectives of the first and second declensions (magnus, a, um); agreement
_source.L8: adjectives of the third declension (gravis, e)
_source.L9: first conjugation: present, imperfect, future indicative active of laudō
_source.L10: the same three tenses of moneō
_source.L12: present system active of the third conjugation (mittō)
_source.L13: present system active of the fourth conjugation
_source.L14: present system indicative of sum; compounds of sum
_source.L15: the perfect system active (perfect, pluperfect, future perfect; all conjugations and fuī)
_source.L16: puer, ager, vir; miser and integer; the possessives meus, tuus, noster, vester
_source.L17-20: present system passive of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th conjugations, one per lesson
_source.L21: the perfect system of the indicative passive
_source.L23: the imperfect subjunctive active; imperfect subjunctive of sum
_source.L29: the passive subjunctive (present, imperfect, and the perfect system)
_source.L36: adjectives with the genitive in -īus and the dative in -ī (ūnus, alius, tōtus…)
_source.L37: -iō verbs: indicative and subjunctive, active and passive
